summary: Codenames: Pictures swaps the word grid for a grid of surreal, densely-illustrated image cards, making clue-giving looser and more associative than the word version. It plays the same as base Codenames but tends to be friendlier for younger players or non-native speakers since it leans on visual rather than verbal association.
praised: Great for kids, families, or mixed-language groups
Whimsical, imaginative artwork sparks creative clues
Fully compatible/combinable with other Codenames sets
criticised: Images can be more ambiguous than words, leading to messier clues
Some feel it's a bit easier/less sharp than the original
Not a huge structural change if you already own base Codenames

interaction.kind: guessing on a shared image grid where mistakes benefit the opposing team
interaction.detail: As in the original, both teams' agents sit on the same board of picture cards, so misreads can advance the opponents or end the game. Most of a turn is still one spymaster crafting a clue for their own team rather than directly reacting to the rival team's play.
interaction.said: carries the same reputation as base Codenames — the tension comes from a wrong guess handing the rival team a card or ending the game via the assassin

scoring.how_you_win: As in base Codenames, there is no score; a team wins the moment it has contacted all of its own picture-agents first, or immediately loses by picking the assassin.
